title: Configuration File Schema
description: Palace configuration file schema for 3D electromagnetic simulations.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: Top-level configuration for the simulation type and output.

Verbose.description: Controls the level of log file printing.

Output.description: Directory path for saving postprocessing outputs. When omitted, results are written to a `postpro` directory relative to the working directory.

Mesh.description: Input mesh file path. An absolute path is recommended. If the provided mesh is nonconformal, it is assumed to come from a previous *Palace* AMR solve, and all mesh preprocessing checks and modifications (for example [CrackInternalBoundaryElements](@ref config-model-crackinternalboundaryelements)) are skipped.

L0.description: Unit, relative to meters, for mesh vertex coordinates. For example, a value of `1.0e-6` means the mesh coordinates are in μm.

Lc.description: Characteristic length scale used for nondimensionalization, specified in mesh length units. This keyword should typically not be specified by the user. If omitted, Palace uses the largest mesh bounding-box dimension, `max_i(bbmax_i - bbmin_i)`. A value of `1.0` will disable nondimensionalization, so that all computations will take place in the same units as the mesh.

RemoveCurvature.description: Project high-order nodes to the mesh surface, removing all curvature before the simulation.

MakeSimplex.description: Convert all mesh elements to simplices (tetrahedra/triangles).

MakeHexahedral.description: Convert all mesh elements to hexahedra.

ReorderElements.description: Reorder mesh elements to improve cache efficiency.

LocalReorder.description: Number the elements of each process along a Hilbert curve through their centroids (one curve through the whole mesh) once the mesh is partitioned, for the cache efficiency of the operators: the edges, faces and degrees of freedom follow the element order. Unlike `ReorderElements`, this keeps the partition (also of the rebalanced adapted meshes) and the refinement of nonconforming adapted meshes, and has no serial cost. Probes on the boundary between elements take the value in the element first in the order of the input mesh. Results change by round-off (the global phase of eigenvectors does not depend on the element order). Conforming meshes refined after their distribution (`Refinement.Nonconformal` false with adaptive refinement, or `Refinement.UniformLevels`), conforming meshes with curved (high-order) nodes, and nonconforming input meshes (such as saved adapted meshes) keep their element order. For driven problems using p-multigrid with an AMS coarse solver, the reordering can increase the number of linear solver iterations; set `"LocalReorder": false` if this happens.

CleanUnusedElements.description: Remove elements not connected to any domain material.

CrackInternalBoundaryElements.description: Duplicate nodes along interior boundaries to decouple the elements on either side ("crack" the mesh). If not specified, the mesh is cracked along interior boundaries with boundary conditions which apply to each side separately, [PMC](@ref config-boundaries-pmc) (or [ZeroCharge](@ref config-boundaries-zerocharge)) and [Absorbing](@ref config-boundaries-absorbing) boundaries, and along [Impedance](@ref config-boundaries-impedance), [RationalImpedance](@ref config-boundaries-rationalimpedance), and [Conductivity](@ref config-boundaries-conductivity) boundaries with `"Crack": true`. If `true`, the mesh is cracked along all interior boundaries with boundary conditions except for lumped ports, with the surface impedance of impedance boundaries split between their two faces (the behavior of previous versions). If `false`, the mesh is never cracked, which is an error for boundaries with `"Crack": true`. Deprecated: the error estimate for adaptive mesh refinement no longer requires cracking the mesh, and cracking is a per-boundary modeling choice for impedance, rational impedance, and conductivity boundaries.

RefineCrackElements.description: Refine elements adjacent to cracked internal boundaries.

CrackDisplacementFactor.description: Displacement factor applied to cracked nodes as a fraction of the local element size.

AddInterfaceBoundaryElements.description: Add boundary elements at interfaces between domains that lack them.

ExportPrerefinedMesh.description: Export the mesh after preprocessing but before AMR refinement.

ReorientTetMesh.description: Reorient tetrahedral elements to ensure positive Jacobians.

Partitioning.description: Path to a mesh partitioning file. If omitted, partitioning is computed automatically.

CurrentDipole.description: Array of current dipole source excitations.

PEC.title: PEC Boundary
PEC.description: Perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary condition: enforces zero tangential electric field. This is a homogeneous Dirichlet condition for frequency/time domain and magnetostatic formulations.

PMC.title: PMC Boundary
PMC.description: Perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) boundary condition: enforces zero tangential magnetic field. This is the natural (homogeneous Neumann) boundary condition; it also imposes symmetry of the electric field across the surface.

Impedance.description: Array of surface impedance boundary conditions. The surface impedance relates the tangential electric and magnetic fields using the parallel combination of the specified resistance, inductance, and capacitance per square.

RationalImpedance.title: Rational Impedance
RationalImpedance.description: Array of rational surface impedance boundary conditions. The per-square surface impedance is an arbitrary rational function of frequency, Zs(s) = N(s)/D(s) with s = iω, specified by the numerator and denominator polynomial coefficients (its zeros and poles). This generalizes [Impedance](@ref config-boundaries-impedance) to any passive lumped-network response. Only available for frequency domain driven, eigenmode, and boundary mode simulations.

Absorbing.title: Absorbing Boundary
Absorbing.description: Farfield absorbing (scattering) boundary conditions. These are artificial boundary conditions applied at farfield boundaries to minimize reflections.

Conductivity.description: Array of finite conductivity surface impedance boundaries. Models the effect of a boundary with non-infinite conductivity for conductors with thickness much larger than the skin depth. Only available for frequency domain driven and eigenmode simulations.

LumpedPort.title: Lumped Port
LumpedPort.description: Array of lumped port boundary conditions. Lumped ports can be specified on boundaries internal to the computational domain.

WavePort.title: Wave Port
WavePort.description: Array of numeric wave port boundary conditions. Wave ports can only be specified on the true boundary of the computational domain (they must be "one-sided"). A 2D boundary mode eigenproblem is solved on each wave port to compute the port mode shape. Only available for frequency domain driven and eigenmode simulations.

FloquetPort.title: Floquet Port
FloquetPort.description: Array of Floquet port boundary conditions for periodic driven simulations. Floquet ports model diffraction gratings and other periodic electromagnetic devices, compute diffraction-order S-parameters, and require [Periodic](@ref config-boundaries-periodic) boundary conditions with two transverse boundary pairs.

WavePortPEC.title: Wave Port PEC
WavePortPEC.description: Additional PEC boundary conditions for the 2D eigensolve used in wave port mode analysis, along with those already specified under [PEC](@ref config-boundaries-pec) and [Conductivity](@ref config-boundaries-conductivity). Only relevant when [WavePort](@ref config-boundaries-waveport) boundaries are present.

SurfaceCurrent.title: Surface Current
SurfaceCurrent.description: Array of surface current source boundaries. Prescribes a unit source surface current excitation on the given boundary to excite a driven, transient, or magnetostatic simulation. For magnetostatic simulations, inductance matrix entries are extracted for each surface current boundary.

FluxLoop.title: Flux Loop
FluxLoop.description: Array of flux loop boundaries for magnetostatic simulations. Prescribes fixed amounts of magnetic flux through holes in metallic planes. The inductance matrix is extracted from the stored magnetic energy.

Superconductor.description: Array of thin-film superconductor sheet boundaries for magnetostatic simulations. Each sheet contributes a London kinetic-inductance term to the extracted total inductance, modeled by the one-sided finite-thickness London kinetic sheet inductance L_ksq = mu0 * lambda * coth(d/lambda) (field on one face, e.g. a film over a ground plane), specified either via the penetration depth and film thickness or directly (as the thin-film limit lambda^2/d when d << lambda). Only available for magnetostatic simulations.

Ground.title: Ground Boundary
Ground.description: Zero-voltage (ground) boundary condition for electrostatic simulations. Mutually exclusive with [PEC](@ref config-boundaries-pec).

ZeroCharge.title: Zero Charge Boundary
ZeroCharge.description: Zero surface charge (homogeneous Neumann) boundary condition for electrostatic simulations. Also imposes symmetry of the electric field across the surface. Mutually exclusive with [PMC](@ref config-boundaries-pmc).

Terminal.description: Array of terminal boundaries for electrostatic simulations. Capacitance matrix entries are extracted for each terminal.

Periodic.title: Periodic Boundary
Periodic.description: Periodic boundary conditions for surfaces whose meshes are identical after translation and/or rotation. Floquet periodic boundary conditions with a phase shift are also supported.

Solver.title: Solver
Solver.description: Solver configuration for all simulation types.

Order.description: Finite element order (degree). Arbitrary high-order spaces are supported.

PartialAssemblyOrder.description: Order at which to switch from full assembly of finite element operators to [partial assembly](https://mfem.org/howto/assembly_levels/). Setting to `1` fully activates partial assembly on all levels; a large value (greater than [Order](@ref config-solver-order)) results in fully assembled sparse matrix operators.

QuadratureOrderJacobian.description: Use the Jacobian-based quadrature order instead of the default.

QuadratureOrderExtra.description: Extra quadrature order added on top of the default.

Device.description: The runtime device configuration passed to [MFEM](https://mfem.org/howto/assembly_levels/) to activate different computation backends. When *Palace* is built with OpenMP support (`PALACE_WITH_OPENMP=ON`), `omp` is automatically added to the MFEM device list.

Backend.description: Specifies the [libCEED backend](https://libceed.org/en/latest/gettingstarted/#backends) to use. If omitted, Palace selects a suitable backend based on [Device](@ref config-solver-device).

Eigenmode.title: Eigenmode Solver
Eigenmode.description: Configuration for the eigenvalue solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Eigenmode"`.

Driven.title: Driven Solver
Driven.description: Configuration for the frequency domain driven solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Driven"`.

Transient.title: Transient Solver
Transient.description: Configuration for the time domain driven solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Transient"`. Simulations always start from rest at *t* = 0.

Electrostatic.title: Electrostatic Solver
Electrostatic.description: Configuration for the electrostatic solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Electrostatic"`.

Magnetostatic.title: Magnetostatic Solver
Magnetostatic.description: Configuration for the magnetostatic solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Magnetostatic"`.

Linear.title: Linear Solver
Linear.description: Configuration for the linear solver used by all simulation types.

oneOf.description: Perform a time-domain excitation response simulation.
Perform an electrostatic analysis to compute the capacitance matrix for a set of voltage terminals.
Perform a magnetostatic analysis to compute the inductance matrix for a set of current sources.
Perform a 2D waveguide boundary mode analysis to compute propagation constants on a cross-section.

Paraview.description: Set to `true` to output fields in [ParaView](https://www.paraview.org/) format.

GridFunction.description: Set to `true` to output fields in MFEM grid function format for visualization with [GLVis](https://glvis.org/).

Refinement.title: Mesh Refinement
Refinement.description: Configuration for adaptive and uniform mesh refinement.

Tol.description: Stop adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) when the norm of the estimated error falls below this value. The error is reported in `error-indicators.csv`.

MaxIts.description: Maximum number of AMR iterations to perform.

MaxSize.description: The maximum allowable number of degrees of freedom for AMR. If an adapted mesh exceeds this value no further adaptation will occur. A value less than 1 means that no maximum size constraint will be imposed.

UpdateFraction.description: Dörfler marking fraction used to specify which elements to refine. This marking strategy will mark the smallest number of elements that make up "UpdateFraction" of the total error in the mesh. A larger value will refine more elements per iteration, at the cost of the final mesh being less efficient.

Nonconformal.description: Use nonconformal refinement in adaptation. Required for non-simplex meshes.

MaxNCLevels.description: Maximum number of nonconformal refinement levels. `0` means no limit.

MaximumImbalance.description: Maximum ratio of elements between the most- and least-loaded MPI ranks before repartitioning.

SaveAdaptIterations.description: Save postprocessing results from each AMR iteration in a subdirectory `iterationX`.

SaveAdaptMesh.description: Save the final adapted mesh to disk.

UniformLevels.description: Levels of uniform parallel mesh refinement to be performed on the input mesh. If not performing AMR, these may be used as levels within a geometric multigrid scheme. If performing AMR the most refined mesh is used as the initial mesh and the coarser meshes cannot be used in a geometric multigrid scheme.

SerialUniformLevels.description: Levels of uniform serial mesh refinement applied before parallel distribution.

Boxes.description: Array of axis-aligned box refinement regions. All elements with a node inside the box are marked for refinement.

Spheres.description: Array of sphere refinement regions. All elements with a node inside the sphere are marked for refinement.

Levels.description: Levels of parallel mesh refinement inside this box region.

BoundingBoxMin.description: Minimum coordinates `[x, y, z]` of the axis-aligned bounding box for this refinement region, in mesh length units.

BoundingBoxMax.description: Maximum coordinates `[x, y, z]` of the axis-aligned bounding box for this refinement region, in mesh length units.

Levels.description: Levels of parallel mesh refinement inside this sphere region.

Radius.description: Radius of the sphere, in mesh length units.

Center.description: Center coordinates `[x, y, z]` of the sphere, in mesh length units.

Permeability.description: Relative permeability for this material. Scalar or vector of 3 coefficients corresponding to each of `"MaterialAxes"`.

Permittivity.description: Relative permittivity for this material. Scalar or vector of 3 coefficients corresponding to each of `"MaterialAxes"`.

LossTan.description: Loss tangent for this material. Scalar or vector of 3 coefficients corresponding to each of `"MaterialAxes"`.

Conductivity.description: Electrical conductivity for this material, S/m. Activates the Ohmic loss model in this domain. Scalar or vector of 3 coefficients corresponding to each of `"MaterialAxes"`.

LondonDepth.description: London penetration depth for this material, specified in mesh length units. Activates the London equations-based model relating superconducting current and electromagnetic fields in this domain.

MaterialAxes.description: Axes directions for specification of anisotropic material properties. Required to be unit length and orthogonal.

Direction.description: Direction of the Dirac current source specifying the dipole. Axis-aligned directions can be specified using keywords: `"+X"`, `"-X"`, `"+Y"`, `"-Y"`, `"+Z"`, `"-Z"`. The direction can alternatively be specified as a normalized array of three values, for example `[0.0, 1.0, 0.0]`.

Energy.description: Array of objects for postprocessing domain energies. Postprocesses the electric and magnetic field energy inside a given domain. Results are written to `domain-E.csv` in the output directory.

Probe.description: Array of probe points for evaluating field values at specified locations in space. The electric field **E** and magnetic flux density **B** are probed and written to `probe-E.csv` and `probe-B.csv` in the output directory.

Crack.description: Crack the mesh along this boundary where it lies in the interior of the computational domain, duplicating the mesh vertices on it. If `true`, the two faces of the sheet are modeled as independent surfaces, each carrying its own current, with no coupling through the sheet: this models a conductor much thicker than its penetration depth, and each face has the given surface impedance, as on an exterior boundary. If `false`, the boundary is a thin sheet with a single tangential electric field on it, which couples the fields on its two sides: this models a film much thinner than its penetration depth, and the given surface impedance is that of the film. Only relevant for interior boundaries.

Attributes.description: Integer array of mesh boundary attributes this object applies to.

PenetrationDepth.description: London penetration depth λ of the superconducting film, specified in mesh length units. Used with Thickness to compute the finite-thickness kinetic sheet inductance L_ksq = mu0 * lambda * coth(d/lambda). Mutually exclusive with KineticInductance.

Thickness.description: Superconducting film thickness d, specified in mesh length units. Used with PenetrationDepth to compute the finite-thickness kinetic sheet inductance L_ksq = mu0 * lambda * coth(d/lambda). Mutually exclusive with KineticInductance.

KineticInductance.description: Kinetic sheet inductance L_ksq, H/sq, specified directly as an alternative to (PenetrationDepth, Thickness). Mutually exclusive with those two.

TwoSided.description: Model the film as a two-port (transfer-matrix) sheet: two coupled coincident faces so the tangential field can jump across it, capturing two-sided screening for d >~ lambda. Requires (PenetrationDepth, Thickness), a 3D mesh, and an interior film. The magnetostatic solution is discontinuous across the film, which is not cracked.

External.description: Whether this boundary is on the exterior of the computational domain, with only one conductor surface. Crack.description: Crack the mesh along this boundary where it lies in the interior of the computational domain, duplicating the mesh vertices on it. If `true`, the two faces of the sheet are modeled as independent conductor surfaces, each carrying its own current with the surface impedance of the conductor, with no coupling through the sheet: this models a conductor much thicker than the skin depth. If `false`, the boundary is a thin sheet with a single tangential electric field on it and the admittance of both conductor surfaces, which couples the fields on its two sides: this models a film thinner than the skin depth. The two models give the same result when the currents on both faces are equal, and differ in the conductor loss (by up to a factor of two) when the current flows on one face only. Only relevant for interior boundaries.

IncludeInSynthesis.description: Controls whether this lumped port contributes a port-mode basis vector to the reduced-order model when adaptive driven circuit synthesis is enabled ([AdaptiveCircuitSynthesis](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptivecircuitsynthesis)). SolverType.description: Eigenvalue solver for computing the boundary mode. Accepts the same options as [`/Solver/Eigenmode/Type`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-type). If omitted, Palace selects the available eigenvalue solver backend.

oneOf.description: Use Palace's default backend selection for the available build.

Excitation.description: Turns on or off port excitation for driven simulations. Can be specified as a boolean or as a non-negative integer (excitation group index). See the [boundary conditions guide](../guide/boundaries.md#Lumped-and-wave-port-excitation) for details.

Active.description: Turns on or off the damping boundary condition for this port for driven simulations.

IncludeInSynthesis.description: Controls whether this wave port contributes a port-mode basis vector to the reduced-order model when adaptive driven circuit synthesis is enabled ([AdaptiveCircuitSynthesis](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptivecircuitsynthesis)). The boundary condition itself is always enforced; only the inclusion of the port mode in the synthesized circuit matrices is affected. Excited ports must always be included; the configuration parser will reject a port with `"Excitation" > 0` and `"IncludeInSynthesis": false`.

MaxIts.description: Maximum number of iterations for the GMRES solver used in the wave port boundary mode analysis.

KSPTol.description: Tolerance for the linear solver used in the wave port boundary mode analysis.

ComplexCoarseSolve.description: Use an exact doubled-real factorization for the wave port boundary mode linear solver. When omitted, inherits [`/Solver/Linear/ComplexCoarseSolve`](@ref config-solver-linear-complexcoarsesolve) if given (the real-valued approximation if it is omitted: the wave port solvers do not choose it at setup) and [`/Solver/Linear/PCMatReal`](@ref config-solver-linear-pcmatreal). An explicit value takes precedence over both: `true` uses the exact factorization and `false` includes the complex terms in the real-valued preconditioner. This override affects only this wave port and does not change the full 3D system preconditioner.

EigenTol.description: Tolerance for the eigenvalue solver used in the wave port boundary mode analysis. In adaptive frequency sweeps, it also sets the acceptance tolerance of the reduced model of the port modes used at the output frequencies (the larger of 10 times this tolerance and the smaller of `1e-4` and 0.01 times [`/Solver/Driven/AdaptiveTol`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptivetol)): a port mode of the reduced model with a larger residual is computed again by the eigenvalue solver. The phases of the S-parameters and of the port voltages and currents need this accuracy: with the default `1e-6`, the port modes of a lossless line can be inaccurate at some output frequencies, which shifts the phases of the transmission coefficients there by up to tenths of a degree. For accurate phases, set `1e-8`, at a moderate cost in adaptive sweeps with many output frequencies; `1e-10` makes the eigenvalue solver compute most port modes at the output frequencies, which can make such sweeps noticeably slower.

MaxSize.description: Maximum subspace dimension for the eigenvalue solver. If omitted, Palace uses `max(2 × Mode, Mode + 15)`.

Verbose.description: Verbosity level for the wave port linear and eigensolvers.

VoltagePath.description: Open path of coordinate points across the port face, specified in mesh length units. Each entry is a floating point array of length equal to the spatial dimension. The path is **directed from the signal (high-potential) terminal to the ground (low-potential) terminal**, matching the lumped-port `"Direction"` convention. When specified, this: 1. Pins the wave-port mode polarity so that ``\int E_{\text{mode}} \cdot dl`` along the path is real-positive (required for consistent S-parameter signs when mixing wave and lumped ports in a driven simulation; without it, cross-type S-parameters may be ``180^\circ`` out of phase). 2. Enables voltage and characteristic impedance ``Z_{PV}`` postprocessing for the wave port. For example, in a coaxial wave port the first point is on the inner conductor (signal) and the last point is on the outer conductor (ground); for a CPW port, the first point is on the center trace and the last point in the gap. The path is projected onto the port plane and split at the port mesh element boundaries, and each piece is integrated with a Gauss-Legendre rule exact for the finite element field on affine elements (triangles, parallelograms), so the voltage is the exact line integral of the discrete field however finely the mesh is refined along the path.

PolarityAttributes.description: Pair of parent-mesh boundary attributes `[signal, ground]` (signal/high-potential terminal first, ground/low-potential terminal second). Same role as the polarity component of [VoltagePath](@ref config-boundaries-waveport-voltagepath): the mode is flipped so that the modal E-field points from the signal attribute toward the ground attribute. Ignored if `"VoltagePath"` is also specified. Lightweight alternative to `"VoltagePath"` when only polarity is needed (no ``Z_{PV}``). Both attributes must be present as distinct boundary attributes in the input mesh, with edges that lie on the port face.

Eigenmode.title: Eigenmode Solver
Eigenmode.description: Configuration for the eigenvalue solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Eigenmode"`.

Target.description: (Nonzero) frequency target above which to search for eigenvalues, GHz.

Tol.description: Relative convergence tolerance for the eigenvalue solver.

MaxIts.description: Maximum number of iterations for the iterative eigenvalue solver. For nonlinear problems, applies to the linear or quadratic eigenvalue solver computing the initial guesses of the `"Hybrid"` solver (see `"NonlinearMaxIts"` for the quasi-Newton iterations), or to the `"SLP"` solver. If omitted, Palace uses `1,000,000` iterations.

MaxSize.description: Maximum subspace dimension for the eigenvalue solver. If omitted, Palace uses `max(3 × N, N + 28)` for `N` ≥ 6 with the SLEPc solver and [`"MinQ"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-minq) > 0.5, which keeps the strongly damped Ritz values that a larger subspace captures from stalling the convergence, except with the `"SLP"` nonlinear solver, and `max(2 × N, N + 15)` otherwise.

N.description: Number of eigenvalues to compute. The SLEPc solver often converges more eigenpairs, which are written to `eig.csv` as well, except with the relaxation of the linear solver tolerance (see [`"LinearSolverRelaxation"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-linearsolverrelaxation)).

Save.description: Number of computed field modes to save to disk for [visualization with ParaView](../guide/postprocessing.md#Visualization). Files are saved in the `paraview/` (and/or `gridfunction/`) directory under [`/Problem/Output`](@ref config-problem-output).

PEPLinear.description: Linearize the polynomial eigenvalue problem before solving.

Scaling.description: Enable scaling of the eigenvalue problem.

StartVector.description: Use a random start vector for the eigensolver.

StartVectorConstant.description: Use a constant start vector instead of a random one.

WarmStart.description: For adaptive mesh refinement, start the eigenvalue solver of each adaptation iteration from the eigenvectors of the previous one: the start vector combines them, transferred to the refined and rebalanced mesh, with a small component of the random (or constant) start vector. Only used with [`"StartVector"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-startvector) and nonconformal refinement ([`/Model/Refinement/Nonconformal`](@ref config-model-refinement-nonconformal)). The eigenvectors are kept in a discontinuous vector L2 space between the iterations. The warm start is skipped when the previous solve converged within its first Krylov cycle, and the linear solves of the first Krylov cycle of a warm-started solve use `1e-2` times [`/Solver/Linear/Tol`](@ref config-solver-linear-tol) (not below `1e-12`).

AdaptiveShift.description: For adaptive mesh refinement, move the shift of the shift-and-invert spectral transformation of each adaptation iteration after the first from the target into the band of the requested eigenvalues of the previous iteration: to `0.45` times the distance from the target to the farthest requested eigenvalue, moved down to the middle of the interval between consecutive eigenvalues when it lies within a quarter of that interval from one of them, and further down to the first interval at least half as wide as the mean spacing of the requested eigenvalues. The search is still for the modes nearest above [`"Target"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-target), which are then the dominant ones of the transformed operator, while the modes below the target, which shift-and-invert at the target makes the most dominant ones, are less dominant than all of them, so that fewer restarts are needed, and the errors of the linear solves enter the eigenvalues far from the target less amplified. The shift stays at the target after a solve which converged within two restarts with it there, as few as a warm-started solve needs. The error estimates are converted to relative errors of the eigenvalues for the convergence test. If the shift is above the middle of the target and the farthest requested eigenvalue found (modes entering the requested set lowered it), the solve is repeated once with the shift from the eigenvalues found, else (or if fewer eigenpairs than requested converge) with the shift at the target. Only used by the SLEPc Krylov-Schur solver for linear problems, and quadratic ones with [`"PEPLinear"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-peplinear), without frequency-dependent boundary conditions.

LinearSolverRelaxation.description: Constant `c` for relaxing the tolerance of the linear solves as the requested eigenpairs converge (inexact shift-and-invert): after each restart of the SLEPc Krylov-Schur solver, the relative tolerance of the linear solver becomes the smallest `c' × Tol / r` over the requested eigenpairs not converged yet, with `r` the error estimate of the eigenpair and `c' = min(c, 0.01 gap / ratio)`, where `gap` is the relative distance of its transformed eigenvalue to the nearest other one and `ratio` that of the largest transformed eigenvalue to its own, bounded by [`/Solver/Linear/Tol`](@ref config-solver-linear-tol) from below and by `1e-4` from above. A solve which ends with fewer converged eigenpairs than requested, with a requested eigenpair accepted although its Ritz value did not settle between restarts, or with a requested eigenpair whose backward error exceeds `2 Tol max(1, |λ - σ| / |σ|)` for the shift `σ` (the residuals of the linear solves enter that of an eigenpair amplified by about `|λ - σ| / |σ|`), is repeated without relaxation. Only the `N` requested eigenpairs are then written to `eig.csv`, since further converged eigenpairs can be less accurate. `0` disables the relaxation. Only used by the SLEPc Krylov-Schur solver (linear problems, and quadratic ones with [`"PEPLinear"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-peplinear)), except with the `"SLP"` nonlinear solver.

LinearSolverDeflation.description: Number of vectors `k` with which the shift-and-invert linear solves are deflated: the first linear solve of each eigenvalue solve provides the `k` harmonic Ritz vectors of the preconditioned operator with the eigenvalues closest to zero, which form the basis `W` of the two-level (A-DEF1) deflation `P r = B (r - A W E⁻¹ Wᴴ r) + W E⁻¹ Wᴴ r`, `E = Wᴴ A W`, of the preconditioner `B` for the later solves. The multigrid preconditioner of shifted Maxwell operators maps a few directions (for example modes close to the target, or high-frequency components which the smoother does not reach) to eigenvalues close to or below zero, which slow down GMRES. The basis takes `2 k` vectors of memory (in single precision on CPUs), and each linear solver iteration `k` more inner products (one global reduction) and `2 k` more vector updates. `-1` chooses the vectors for each eigenvalue solve: only harmonic Ritz values of magnitude below 0.25 are deflated at first (at most 64, possibly none), and only if GMRES for the projected preconditioned operator predicts that the deflation saves at least 5% at its measured cost; a solve without deflation after 8 and then every 32 deflated solves verifies the gain (the deflation stops, or goes back to fewer vectors, if it finds none), and while the deflation pays, the vectors of the values below 0.5 and then 1 from the same first solve are tried (when the model predicts at least 10% fewer iterations with them), each set kept if it saves more than 3% over the previous one on the same right-hand side. `0` disables the deflation (the default: deflation can shift the eigenvalues of modes far from the shift by more than the tolerance, which their backward errors do not show). Only used with GMRES with left preconditioning.

MinQ.description: Minimum quality factor `Q = |ω| / (2 Im{ω})` of the eigenmodes searched for in problems with damping: strongly damped modes with lower `Q`, and growing modes with `|Q|` < 10, are excluded from the search region, so that their Ritz values, which converge slowly, cannot stall the convergence of the others. Values ≤ 0.5 disable the restriction (every damped mode has `Q` ≥ 0.5). Only used by the SLEPc solver, except with the `"SLP"` nonlinear solver.

IntermediateTol.description: Relative convergence tolerance for the eigenvalue solver in the adaptation iterations before the last one, whose eigenvectors only drive the mesh refinement (see [`/Model/Refinement`](@ref config-model-refinement)). The last iteration, known from [`/Model/Refinement/MaxIts`](@ref config-model-refinement-maxits) and [`/Model/Refinement/MaxSize`](@ref config-model-refinement-maxsize), uses [`"Tol"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-tol); when the error indicator ends the adaptation earlier ([`/Model/Refinement/Tol`](@ref config-model-refinement-tol)), the solve is repeated on the final mesh with the final tolerances. The results of the intermediate iterations (written with [`/Model/Refinement/SaveAdaptIterations`](@ref config-model-refinement-saveadaptiterations)) are only as accurate as these tolerances. Looser tolerances can change the refinement slightly, and therefore the final mesh and results. If omitted, Palace uses `"Tol"`, and values below it have no effect. See also [`"IntermediateLinearSolverTol"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-intermediatelinearsolvertol).

IntermediateLinearSolverTol.description: Relative tolerance of the linear solver in the adaptation iterations before the last one, see [`"IntermediateTol"`](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-intermediatetol). If omitted, Palace uses [`/Solver/Linear/Tol`](@ref config-solver-linear-tol), and values below it have no effect.

A positive value ensures the reduced-order model is reliable relative to the full-order model in the frequency band of interest.

AdaptiveMaxSamples.description: Maximum number of frequency samples used to construct the reduced-order model for adaptive sweep, if the tolerance (`"AdaptiveTol"`) is not met first. In simulations with multiple excitations, this is the maximum per excitation.

AdaptiveConvergenceMemory.description: Number of consecutive samples satisfying the error tolerance required to declare convergence of the adaptive sampling algorithm.

AdaptivePoleExclusion.description: Relative half-width `w` of the frequency intervals that adaptive sampling excludes from its search for the frequency with the largest error of the reduced-order model: the intervals `[(1 - w) f, (1 + w) f]` around the real part `f` of each pole of the reduced-order model narrower than them (quality factor above `1 / (2 w)`), once it has converged: moved since the previous sample by less than [`"AdaptiveTol"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptivetol) times the half-width. Within a resonance much narrower than the sampling of the sweep, such as a weakly coupled mode of quality factor `1e6` to `1e11`, the reduced-order model error cannot be reduced below [`"AdaptiveTol"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptivetol), and samples there only restart the count of [`"AdaptiveConvergenceMemory"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptiveconvergencememory). The frequencies of the sweep in the excluded intervals are still searched. Only used for reduced-order models without frequency-dependent boundary conditions (such as wave ports or surface conductivity). `0.0` disables the exclusion. Off by default (`0`): with adaptive mesh refinement, the excluded samples are also missing from the error indicator, which changes the refinement path, unless [`"AdaptiveIndicatorSamples"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptiveindicatorsamples) computes it at fixed frequencies.

AdaptiveIndicatorSamples.description: With adaptive mesh refinement, the number of frequencies of the sweep, uniformly spaced in the sample index from the first to the last one, at which the adaptive frequency sweep computes the error indicator from the reduced-order model after its sampling, instead of from its full-order samples. The full-order samples follow the greedy search for the largest reduced-order model error, whose choices change with round-off (process count, build), and the indicator of the refinement, which averages the error over them, changes with them: with fixed frequencies, the marked elements no longer depend on the sample set, and [`"AdaptivePoleExclusion"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptivepoleexclusion) does not change the refinement either. The reduced-order model solutions are within [`"AdaptiveTol"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptivetol) of the full-order ones. The cost is one error estimate per frequency and excitation, as for each full-order sample otherwise. The fixed frequencies under-weight the resonances narrower than their spacing, and the refinement then does not converge those modes (see [`"AdaptiveIndicatorMaxQ"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptiveindicatormaxq)). The error indicator norm of each adaptation iteration, which the refinement [`"Tol"`](@ref config-model-refinement-tol) is compared with, is then the root mean square over these frequencies, which can be well below the one over the full-order samples (which sit on the resonances). `0`, the default, uses the full-order samples.

AdaptiveIndicatorMaxQ.description: With [`"AdaptiveIndicatorSamples"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptiveindicatorsamples) greater than `0`, the error indicator is also computed at the resonances of the reduced-order model in the band of the sweep with a quality factor below this value. The fixed frequencies only weigh a resonance narrower than their spacing when one of them falls within a few linewidths. Weakly coupled resonances, of larger quality factors, satisfy the full-order equations only when the sampling happens to visit them, which would make the indicator depend on the samples again: keep the value well below their quality factors, e.g. `1e5` when they are `1e6` and more. The resonances are the poles of the reduced-order model whose eigenvectors satisfy the full-order equations to `1e-2` relative to the size of their terms (the projection also has spurious poles, which change with the samples and leave residuals of order one). Each weighs in the indicator as much as the fixed frequencies together: a single field among theirs does not drive the refinement. The candidates are listed in the log with their residuals; the poles are not computed with frequency-dependent boundary conditions (wave or Floquet ports, second-order farfield, surface conductivity or rational surface impedance boundaries), for which the log warns. `0.0`, the default, adds none.

CoarseReuseTol.description: Relative frequency distance within which the linear solver of a frequency sweep reuses the coarse-level sparse direct factorization of the multigrid preconditioner computed at an earlier frequency, instead of factoring the coarse level again. A solve with a reused factorization still converges to [`/Linear/Tol`](@ref config-solver-linear-tol); when it needs 50% more iterations than the solve at the factored frequency, the coarse level is factored again and the solve continues. Only used when the preconditioner is geometric multigrid with more than one level (see [`/Linear/MGMaxLevels`](@ref config-solver-linear-mgmaxlevels)). An explicit value applies to both uniform and adaptive sweeps, and `0.0` disables reuse. If omitted, Palace uses `0.05` for uniform sweeps and `0.0` for adaptive sweeps ([`"AdaptiveTol"`](@ref config-solver-driven-adaptivetol) > 0), whose samples are rarely that close and whose choice of samples a different coarse solve can change.

AdaptiveGSOrthogonalization.description: Gram-Schmidt variant for orthogonalizing the adaptive reduced-order model basis. Same options as [`/Linear/GSOrthogonalization`](@ref config-solver-linear-gsorthogonalization).

AdaptiveCircuitSynthesis.description: Use the adaptive reduced-order model to print synthesized circuit-like matrices (L⁻¹, R⁻¹, C). Requires adaptive sweep to be enabled, all `LumpedPort` fields to be orthogonal, and only LRC-type frequency dependence (no `WavePort`, `Conductivity`, `RationalImpedance`, or second-order farfield BCs).

AdaptiveCircuitSynthesisDomainOrthogonal.description: Weight matrix type for domain orthogonalization when building synthesized circuit matrices.

SamplesPoint.title: Point Samples
SamplesPoint.description: Explicit list of frequency sample points.

SaveStep.description: Save fields every N steps within this sample. `0` disables saving.

AddToPROM.description: Force inclusion of these points in the PROM for adaptive sweep (primarily a debugging tool).

FreqStep.description: Step size, GHz. Mutually exclusive with `"NSample"`.

NSample.description: Number of samples, the first at `"MinFreq"` (a single sample is `"MinFreq"`). Mutually exclusive with `"FreqStep"`.

SaveStep.description: Save fields every N steps. `0` disables saving.

AddToPROM.description: Force inclusion in the PROM for adaptive sweep.

NSample.description: Number of samples, the first at `"MinFreq"` (a single sample is `"MinFreq"`).

SaveStep.description: Save fields every N steps. `0` disables saving.

AddToPROM.description: Force inclusion in the PROM for adaptive sweep.

Transient.title: Transient Solver
Transient.description: Configuration for the time domain driven solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Transient"`. Simulations always start from rest at *t* = 0.

Type.description: Time integration scheme for the second-order ODE system.

Excitation.description: Controls the time dependence of the source excitation.

ExcitationFreq.description: Center frequency for harmonic source excitations, GHz. Only relevant when `"Excitation"` is `"Sinusoidal"`, `"Gaussian"`, `"DifferentiatedGaussian"`, or `"ModulatedGaussian"`.

ExcitationWidth.description: Pulse width for Gaussian-type source excitations, ns. Only relevant when `"Excitation"` is `"Gaussian"`, `"DifferentiatedGaussian"`, `"ModulatedGaussian"`, or `"SmoothStep"`.

MaxTime.description: End of simulation time interval, ns.

SaveStep.description: Controls how often, in number of time steps, to save computed fields to disk for [visualization with ParaView](../guide/postprocessing.md#Visualization). Files are saved in the `paraview/` (and/or `gridfunction/`) directory under [`/Problem/Output`](@ref config-problem-output).

Order.description: Order of adaptive Runge-Kutta integrators or maximum multistep method order, must be within `[2, 5]`. Only relevant when `"Type"` is `"ARKODE"` or `"CVODE"`.

RelTol.description: Relative tolerance for adaptive time-stepping. Only relevant when `"Type"` is `"ARKODE"` or `"CVODE"`.

AbsTol.description: Absolute tolerance for adaptive time-stepping. Only relevant when `"Type"` is `"ARKODE"` or `"CVODE"`.

BoundaryMode.title: Boundary Mode Solver
BoundaryMode.description: Configures the 2D boundary mode analysis solver, which computes propagation constants of guided modes on a waveguide cross-section. Used when [Type](@ref config-problem-type) is `"BoundaryMode"`.

Freq.description: Operating frequency for the mode analysis, GHz.

Save.description: Number of computed field modes to save to disk for [visualization with ParaView](../guide/postprocessing.md#Visualization). Files are saved in the `paraview/` (and/or `gridfunction/`) directory under the directory specified by [Output](@ref config-problem-output).

Target.description: Target effective index ``n_\text{eff} = k_n / k_0`` for the eigenvalue solver shift-and-invert spectral transformation, where ``k_n`` is the propagation constant of the guided mode and ``k_0 = \omega / c_0`` is the free-space wavenumber. When specified, the solver searches for modes with effective index near this value. If omitted, Palace computes the shift from material properties as `k_n = (ω / c_min) × sqrt(1.1)`, where `c_min` is the minimum material light speed in the solve domain.

Tol.description: Relative convergence tolerance for the eigenvalue solver.

MaxSize.description: Maximum subspace dimension for the eigenvalue solver. If omitted, Palace uses `max(2 × N, N + 15)`.

Type.description: Specifies the eigenvalue solver to be used for the mode analysis. See [Eigenmode Type](@ref config-solver-eigenmode-type).

Attributes.description: Integer array of 3D mesh boundary attributes from which to extract a 2D cross-section submesh for the mode analysis. When specified, the input mesh must be 3D and a standalone 2D submesh is extracted from these boundary faces. When not specified, the input mesh is used directly and must be 2D.

Electrostatic.title: Electrostatic Solver
Electrostatic.description: Configuration for the electrostatic solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Electrostatic"`.

Save.description: Number of computed electric field solutions to save to disk for [visualization with ParaView](../guide/postprocessing.md#Visualization), ordered by the entries in the computed capacitance matrix. Files are saved in the `paraview/` (and/or `gridfunction/`) directory under [`/Problem/Output`](@ref config-problem-output).

Magnetostatic.title: Magnetostatic Solver
Magnetostatic.description: Configuration for the magnetostatic solver. Only relevant when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Magnetostatic"`.

Save.description: Number of computed magnetic field solutions to save to disk for [visualization with ParaView](../guide/postprocessing.md#Visualization), ordered by excitation: the surface current sources in index order, then the flux loop excitations in excitation index order (the entries of the computed inductance matrix when each is a single source). Files are saved in the `paraview/` (and/or `gridfunction/`) directory under [`/Problem/Output`](@ref config-problem-output).

InactivePorts.description: Global default boundary condition applied to inactive surface current ports during the inductance matrix sweep. During the sweep each surface current port is excited one at a time; this option controls how the remaining (inactive) ports are treated. Individual ports can override this via [`/Boundaries/SurfaceCurrent`](@ref config-boundaries-surfacecurrent) `"InactiveMode"`.

Linear.title: Linear Solver
Linear.description: Configuration for the linear solver used by all simulation types.

Type.description: Specifies the solver used for preconditioning the linear system. If omitted, Palace selects BoomerAMG for electrostatic problems, AMS for magnetostatic and transient problems, and otherwise the first available sparse direct solver among STRUMPACK, SuperLU_DIST, and MUMPS (AMS if none is available).

KSPType.description: Specifies the iterative Krylov subspace solver. If omitted, Palace uses CG for electrostatic, magnetostatic, and transient simulations, and GMRES otherwise.

Tol.description: Relative residual convergence tolerance for the iterative linear solver.

AbsTol.description: Absolute residual convergence tolerance for the iterative linear solver. The solver converges when `||r|| <= max(Tol * ||b||, AbsTol)`. A value of 0.0 disables the absolute tolerance.

MaxIts.description: Maximum number of iterations for the iterative linear solver.

MaxSize.description: Maximum Krylov space size for GMRES/FGMRES. If omitted, Palace uses [`MaxIts`](@ref config-solver-linear-maxits).

StagnationIts.description: GMRES/FGMRES stop when the residual norm decreased by less than the relative fraction [`StagnationTol`](@ref config-solver-linear-stagnationtol) over the last `StagnationIts` iterations: the solve has reached the accuracy attainable for the preconditioned system, and further iterations would not change the solution. `0` disables the test.

StagnationTol.description: Relative residual decrease over [`StagnationIts`](@ref config-solver-linear-stagnationits) iterations below which GMRES/FGMRES stop.

InitialGuess.description: Use the previous solution as an initial guess for the iterative solver. For adaptive frequency sweeps, the initial guess of each sampled solve is the reduced-order model solution at that frequency. If omitted, Palace enables this for driven simulations, transient simulations, electrostatics, and magnetostatics, and disables it otherwise.

MGMaxLevels.description: When greater than 1, enables [geometric multigrid preconditioning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multigrid_method) using p- and h-multigrid coarsening. The solver specified by `"Type"` is used on the coarsest level; fine levels use Chebyshev smoothing. If omitted, Palace uses `1` for boundary mode analysis (multigrid disabled) and `100` otherwise.

MGCoarsenType.description: Coarsening strategy for constructing p-multigrid levels.

MGUseMesh.description: Use the mesh hierarchy for h-multigrid coarsening.

MGAuxiliarySmoother.description: Use an auxiliary space smoother on multigrid levels. If omitted, Palace disables this for electrostatic and magnetostatic simulations and enables it otherwise. Magnetostatic simulations with `"Superconductor"` or `"FluxLoop"` boundaries enable it when `"LondonPCShift"` is positive.

MGCycleIts.description: Number of V-cycle iterations per preconditioner application for multigrid preconditioners (when geometric multigrid is enabled or `"Type"` is `"AMS"` or `"BoomerAMG"`). If omitted, Palace uses `2` for AMS frequency-domain problems (`"Type"` is `"AMS"` for eigenmode or driven simulations) and `1` otherwise.

MGSmoothIts.description: Number of pre- and post-smooth iterations for multigrid preconditioners, when the geometric multigrid preconditioner is enabled.

MGSmoothOrder.description: Polynomial smoothing order for geometric multigrid. If omitted, Palace uses `max(2 × solution order, 4)`, except when [`/Problem/Type`](@ref config-problem-type) is `"Eigenmode"` and the solution order is 2: then, order 8 is used on multigrid levels whose shifted operator is estimated at setup to be nearly positive semi-definite. Order 8 is not used if a short GMRES probe with the multigrid preconditioner at setup predicts that it needs more iterations than the base order.

MGAuxiliarySmoothOrder.description: Polynomial smoothing order in the auxiliary (gradient) space of the distributive relaxation smoother for geometric multigrid, which is used with [`"MGAuxiliarySmoother"`](@ref config-solver-linear-mgauxiliarysmoother). If omitted, Palace uses `max(2 × solution order, 4)` with [`ComplexCoarseSolve`](@ref config-solver-linear-complexcoarsesolve), where this order needs no more linear solver iterations than the order of the primary space smoother and makes each iteration cheaper, and the order of the primary space smoother (see [`"MGSmoothOrder"`](@ref config-solver-linear-mgsmoothorder)) otherwise.

MGSmoothEigScaleMax.description: Maximum eigenvalue scale for the Chebyshev smoother.

MGSmoothEigScaleMin.description: Minimum eigenvalue scale for the Chebyshev smoother.

MGSmoothSinglePrecision.description: For frequency domain and transient simulations on CPUs, apply the operator of each geometric multigrid level to the search directions of its Chebyshev smoother through single-precision element matrices, and store the element matrices of the auxiliary space operators in single precision. The residuals of the smoothed iterates are computed in double precision, as are the coarsest level and the system matrix, so the preconditioner changes at the level of single-precision rounding. Imaginary volume terms below single-precision accuracy relative to the real part, such as dielectric loss tangents below `1e-6`, are left out of the single-precision applications. The element matrices take additional memory and setup time (about 5 kB and 0.2 ms per tetrahedron at order 3, 16 kB and 0.5 ms at order 4).

MGAuxiliaryResidual.description: Residuals of the iterates between the primary and auxiliary space smoothers of the distributive relaxation smoother (see `"MGAuxiliarySmoother"`).

MGSliverAngle.description: Tetrahedra with a minimum dihedral angle below this value (in degrees) are treated as slivers by geometric multigrid: on every level above the coarsest, the true dofs of the mesh entities around each sliver (see `"MGSliverLayers"`) form a patch, and an exact solve with the dense block of the level operator on each patch precedes the coarse-grid correction. The Chebyshev smoothers, with their diagonal scaling, cannot correct the local modes of a degenerate element, which can then dominate the number of linear solver iterations. Meshes without slivers are not affected. `0.0` disables the patch solves. A negative value (the default) uses 2 degrees for the complex-valued operators of frequency domain driven and eigenmode simulations, and no patch solves for the real-valued operators of electrostatic, magnetostatic and transient simulations (whose conjugate gradient iterations they do not reduce). Larger thresholds can select anisotropic elements, which do not slow down the smoothers, at the cost of many patch solves.

MGSliverLayers.description: Extent of the sliver patches of `"MGSliverAngle"`: `1` for the mesh entities incident to the vertices of the sliver, `0` for its own edges, faces and interior, `-1` for the former unless their dense solves are expensive compared with the smoothing of the multigrid level (on a process, the sum of the squared patch sizes above 12 times its number of true dofs times the order of the Chebyshev smoother, as for large merged clusters of slivers), and no patch solves on the level otherwise.

PCMatReal.description: When `true`, builds the preconditioner for frequency domain problems using a real-valued approximation of the system matrix. Always used on the coarsest multigrid level regardless of this setting.

PCMatShifted.description: When `true`, builds the preconditioner using a positive-definite approximation by flipping the sign of the mass matrix contribution. Can improve performance at high frequencies relative to the lowest nonzero eigenfrequencies of the model. If omitted, Palace enables this for driven simulations using AMS and for boundary mode simulations with multigrid enabled, and disables it otherwise.

ComplexCoarseSolve.description: When `true`, uses the true complex-valued system matrix for the coarse-level solver. When `false`, uses the real-valued approximation (the sum of the real and imaginary parts). If omitted, eigenmode simulations on Linux whose coarse-level solver is `"STRUMPACK"` on the host, with fourth-kind Chebyshev smoothers, use the approximation unless, at the setup of the multigrid preconditioner, a short GMRES probe on the coarse level finds it to be a poor approximation of the complex-valued coarse operator and a short GMRES probe with the whole multigrid cycle predicts that the complex-valued matrix needs at least 1.5 times fewer iterations: they then factorize the complex-valued matrix, which keeps about three times the memory of the real-valued factorization and peaks higher. It is not tried if it is estimated not to fit in the memory available to the process, or if that is unknown. The choice is reused for the later shifts and adaptive mesh refinement iterations. Other simulations and coarse-level solvers (`"SuperLU"`, `"MUMPS"`) use the approximation unless this is `true`.

DropSmallEntries.description: When `true`, drops entries smaller than double-precision machine epsilon from the system matrix used in the sparse direct solver.

ReorderingReuse.description: Reuse the matrix reordering from the previous solve.

PCSide.description: Preconditioning side. If omitted, Palace uses the chosen iterative solver's preconditioning side. Not all options are available for all iterative solver choices.

ColumnOrdering.description: Column ordering algorithm for sparse direct solvers. If omitted, Palace orders `"STRUMPACK"` problems of at least 50000 rows in parallel when STRUMPACK is built with PT-Scotch (PT-Scotch separators on at most 256 processes, METIS for the subgraph of each process) and otherwise uses the sparse direct solver's default ordering. `"STRUMPACK-MP"` ignores it and always orders with METIS.

STRUMPACKCompressionType.description: STRUMPACK compression type. `"STRUMPACK-MP"` ignores it and does not compress.

STRUMPACKLossyPrecision.description: Precision bits for STRUMPACK ZFP lossy compression.

STRUMPACKButterflyLevels.description: Number of butterfly levels for STRUMPACK HODLR compression.

STRUMPACKSelectiveInversion.description: Store the inverses of the separator blocks of the distributed fronts of STRUMPACK (selective inversion), so that the solves with a factorization use matrix products instead of distributed triangular solves; blocks with a 1-norm condition number above 9e10 keep their triangular solves. The inverses add about 10-30% to the time of each factorization and pay off only over many solves with it. If omitted, Palace enables this for eigenmode, boundary mode, and transient simulations, and disables it for driven, electrostatic, and magnetostatic simulations, where each factorization serves the Krylov solve of one frequency or of the sources. Has an effect only with a STRUMPACK built with Palace's selective inversion patch (superbuild or Spack), and none with `"STRUMPACK-MP"`, which never applies the selective inversion.

SuperLU3DCommunicator.description: Use a 3D process grid communicator for SuperLU_DIST.

AMSSingularOperator.description: Indicate to AMS that the operator is singular (e.g. magnetostatics with no essential boundary conditions). If omitted, Palace enables this for magnetostatic simulations and disables it otherwise.

LondonPCShift.description: Preconditioner-only gauge shift for magnetostatic problems with a London (superconductor) sheet term. Adds this multiple of the reluctance-weighted volume mass to the preconditioner matrix only (leaving the operator, solution, and extracted inductance unchanged) to lift the residual gradient null space so AMS is SPD-solvable in parallel. Ignored when no London sheet term is present.

AMGAggressiveCoarsening.description: Enable aggressive coarsening in BoomerAMG. If omitted, Palace enables this for electrostatic, magnetostatic, and transient simulations, and disables it otherwise.

AMSMaxIts.description: Number of AMS iterations per preconditioner application when geometric multigrid is enabled (`"MGMaxLevels"` > 1). If omitted, Palace uses [`/Solver/Order`](@ref config-solver-order).

AMSSmoothIts.description: Number of smoothing sweeps on the Nédélec space in each AMS iteration when AMS is the coarse solver of geometric multigrid (`"MGMaxLevels"` > 1). If omitted, Palace uses 8 when [`"AMSSingularOperator"`](@ref config-solver-linear-amssingularoperator) is enabled (by default, magnetostatic simulations without superconductor boundaries) and [`"MGSmoothIts"`](@ref config-solver-linear-mgsmoothits) otherwise.

DivFreeTol.description: Relative tolerance for divergence-free cleaning used in the eigenmode simulation type. Ignored when a nonzero Floquet wave vector is specified or when a nonzero [LondonDepth](@ref config-domains-materials-londondepth) is used.

DivFreeMaxIts.description: Maximum number of iterations for divergence-free cleaning. Ignored under the same conditions as `"DivFreeTol"`.

EstimatorTol.description: Relative tolerance for the flux projection solve used in the error estimate calculation. The error of the projections adds about this much to the error indicator, which is relative to the energy of the solution, so the tolerance must be well below the indicator norms that matter: adaptive mesh refinement then marks the same elements as with tighter tolerances, up to elements at the marking threshold. If omitted, Palace uses the smaller of `1e-4` and 0.01 times [`/Model/Refinement/Tol`](@ref config-model-refinement-tol), but not less than `1e-10`: that is `1e-4` for the default refinement tolerance `1e-2`, so that the indicator can reach the refinement tolerance unless that is below about `1e-9`. Very accurate solutions (for example of high order on smooth problems), whose indicator norm is within about an order of magnitude of the tolerance, need a tighter value, such as `1e-8` or `1e-10`: the indicator then measures the error of the projections instead of the discretization error.

EstimatorMaxIts.description: Maximum number of iterations for the flux projection solve used in the error estimate calculation.

EstimatorMG.description: When `true`, uses a multigrid preconditioner with AMG coarse solve for the error estimator linear solver. When `false`, and always for the flux recovery on meshes with uncracked interior boundaries with boundary conditions, which is discontinuous across them, the solver uses an entity-block Jacobi preconditioner in CPU builds without OpenMP when the mass matrix is partially assembled (see [PartialAssemblyOrder](@ref config-solver-partialassemblyorder)), for H(div) and H(curl) recovery spaces of [Order](@ref config-solver-order) two and three on meshes made of tetrahedra, prisms, or both, or of triangles, and of order four on meshes made only of tetrahedra or only of triangles, and Jacobi otherwise.

AlwaysComputeErrorEstimation.description: When `true`, computes the flux-recovery error indicator after each solve even without adaptive mesh refinement, and writes it to `error-indicators.csv` and to the `Indicator` (ParaView) or `indicator` (grid function) field of the final output. Adaptive mesh refinement ([`/Model/Refinement/MaxIts`](@ref config-model-refinement-maxits) > 0, except for transient simulations, which do not support it) computes it for every solve except the one after the last refinement allowed by `MaxIts`, which ends the adaptation whatever its value; `true` computes it there as well, so that the final mesh is checked against [`/Model/Refinement/Tol`](@ref config-model-refinement-tol).

GSOrthogonalization.description: Gram-Schmidt variant used to orthogonalize vectors in Krylov subspace methods and other parts of the solver. With `"CGS2"`, GMRES and FGMRES reorthogonalize each basis vector one iteration late, in the same two passes over the basis as the first projection of the next vector, with one global reduction per iteration.
